verdict: Datadog grew revenue 32% to $1.01B and stayed profitable on a GAAP basis — net income more than doubled to $53M — but stock pay of $197M still dwarfs the $7M of GAAP operating income.

segments.name: Platform subscriptions
segments.note: One integrated platform — monitoring, security and AI observability, priced per host and per feature. Datadog reports a single revenue stream.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI features — by far the biggest running cost.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling to engineering and security teams at large companies.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference.

takeaways.title: Growth stayed strong
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 32% to $1,006M, and customers spending $100k+ a year rose 21% to about 4,550 — big companies keep expanding their use of Datadog.

takeaways.title: Cash keeps piling up
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $289M — 29 cents per revenue dollar — and cash plus investments reached $4.8B, because subscriptions are paid upfront and stock pay costs no cash.

takeaways.title: Two margins, one gap
takeaways.text: GAAP operating margin was 1%; non-GAAP was 22%. Almost the entire gap is stock-based compensation — pay delivered in shares rather than cash.

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation was $197M in the quarter, and G&A included $0.7M of M&A transaction costs.
otherDetail: Other income of $52M, net — $55M of interest income and other income, minus $3M of interest expense on Datadog's convertible notes.
